newsitem.title: USA: REPUBLIC SUES TOYOTA MOTOR U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: REPUBLIC SUES TOYOTA MOTOR U.S. UNIT.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc said Tuesday it sued Toyota Motor Corp's unit Toyota Motor Sales USA in an Alabama state court, charging Toyota with unfair and deceptive trade practices.

A Republic spokesman said the company filed the suit in the Circuit Court of Green County, Ala., claiming the unit interfered illegally in its proposed acquisition of one Lexus and two Toyota dealerships from Dobbs Automotive Group in Alabama.

"Toyota has a series of internal policies that limit the number of dealerships any outside dealer can acquire to seven Toyota and three Lexus stores," the Republic spokesman said. "In addition, the policies hold that no single buyer can acquire more than one store every nine months."
"Basically, they have designed a little poison pill," the spokesman said, adding it would take a buyer five years to buy seven Toyota dealerships.

Republic also said Appleway Toyota of Spokane, Wash., filed a complaint with the Washington State Department of Motor Vehicles, charging that Toyota's policies interfere with the proposed sale of Appleway to Republic.
Republic said the Alabama suit seeks an injunction preventing Toyota from using its policies to interfere with the proposed acquisition and the award of compensatory and punitive damages.
